technology_rules: native labels are always preserved alongside the normalized family
hybrid is a structural flag (more than one resource), never inferred from a compound fuel string
dual_fuel is a separate flag (one resource, several fuels) and must not produce a hybrid
ERCOT storage is identified by Technology=BA, never by Fuel

source_backed: active requested MW per named field
queue growth over time (ERCOT only, from 99 vintages)
derived_defensible: withdrawals and MW withdrawn (pjm, miso, caiso, iso-ne, nyiso)
projects and MW reaching operation (same five)
completion rate by submission cohort (same five)
active MW by market with one declared MW semantic
not_defensible: any ERCOT operational or completion metric
completion rate as operational divided by currently active
completion rate for a cohort younger than the observed median time to operation

denominator_rule: completion rate is a cohort metric: of requests submitted in year Y, the share that reached actual commercial operation by the observation date, published with the cohort year and observation window. Never operational divided by currently active. Cohorts younger than the observed median time to operation are censored and must not be published.

contradicted_assumptions: shows all seven markets, but SPP cannot be displayed
one queuedGw per market, but there are seven incompatible MW definitions
a load-versus-generation toggle for every market, but only NYISO publishes a load queue in these artifacts
a medianWaitMonths for every market, which is not defensible for ERCOT

blockers: SPP is rights-blocked for public display under the commercial-publication carve-out
ERCOT publishes no actual commercial-operation date, so completion and time-to-operation exclude ERCOT
CAISO active count (267 rows, 74 GW) must be confirmed against the full queue before publication
ISO-NE active count (60 rows) must be confirmed against the IRTT default filter
PJM queue is split across two files with different schemas; the cycle file covers TC1 only
NYISO historical vintages are not indexed
MISO status is a three-field tuple that cannot be flattened without loss
no market publishes coordinates, so no source is map-ready
